blurb: Fault mechanics, seismic waves, magnitude and moment, earthquake statistics, seismic hazard and engineering.

pics.alt: World map with 358,214 earthquake epicentres from 1963 to 1998 plotted as black dots, outlining the plate boundaries
pics.caption: Preliminary determinations of 358,214 epicentres recorded from 1963 to 1998. The narrow bands along mid-ocean ridges and the broad belts at subduction zones and the Alpine–Himalayan collision zone trace the boundaries of the tectonic plates.
pics.title: Quake epicenters 1963-98.png

pics.alt: Cross-section of the Earth showing curved P, S, PKP, SKS, PP and other seismic ray paths through the crust, mantle and core
pics.caption: Schematic seismic ray paths through the Earth's interior. P (solid) and S (dashed) waves curve as velocity increases with depth; S waves cannot cross the liquid outer core but can convert to P waves there (K) and back, producing phases such as SKS and SKP; P waves that cross the core produce PKP.
pics.title: Earthquake wave paths.svg
